court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: IInd Family Court, Bandra, Mumbai (Petition No.A-739 of 2009)
case_name: Mr. Samit Subhash Agarwal vs Ms. Kamlesh Laltaprasad Gupta
facts_of_case: The Appellant-husband sought a decree of nullity of his marriage with the Respondent-wife. The Respondent-wife filed a counter claim seeking a decree of restitution of conjugal rights. The Family Court dismissed the Petition and allowed the counter claim.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized without the free will and consent of both parties is a nullity.
legal_principles.held: Looking to all these facts, it is contended by the Appellant that his so called marriage with the Respondent has taken place by force and without his free will and consent and is therefore a nullity under the provisions of Hindu Marriage Act 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A party's consent to a marriage can be inferred from their conduct and actions.
legal_principles.held: The Respondent categorically stated that the marriage of the Appellant and the Respondent was solemnized with the free will and consent of the Appellant

outcome.final_order: The Appellant's appeal was allowed, and the trial court's order was set aside.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for nullity of marriage under Hindu Marriage Act
